sourcedFrom: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Remington® V3™ Autoloading Shotguns — 410252 REV 0526 (2016)
cleanIntro: The V3's VersaPort gas system sits in a block at the chamber end, not out under the fore-end, so the field strip is barrel off and two gas pistons out of the top of the block. Which fastener holds those pistons in depends on your stock: a synthetic-stocked V3 has gas compensation plugs, a walnut-stocked one has gas exhaust tubes, and the addendum bound into the front of this manual replaces the manual's own step for the walnut gun. Trigger plate, bolt and bolt disassembly are the Deep Clean branch.

steps.title: Safety button hard right until the red band disappears
steps.action: Push the safety button at the rear of the trigger guard to the shooter's right until the button stops and the red band marking cannot be seen.
steps.prose: The V3 uses a cross-bolt button and reads by colour: red visible means the gun will fire. Push it until it physically stops rather than until it looks pushed — a button part way across is neither on nor off, and there is no detent to tell you by feel. One thing to know before you trust the colour: the manual notes the factory can reverse the safety for a left-handed shooter, and on a reversed gun the ON and OFF sides are exactly opposite to what the book describes.
steps.quote: To engage the safety mechanism, push the “Safety Button,” located at the rear of the trigger guard, to the shooter’s right until the button stops and THE RED BAND MARKING CANNOT BE SEEN. See Picture 4.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Remington® V3™ Autoloading Shotguns — 410252 REV 0526 — Important Parts of the Firearm — The Safety Mechanism, p.8
steps.warn: Remington: the firearm will discharge when the trigger is pulled and the safety mechanism is OFF or in the "Fire" position.

steps.title: Walnut stock or synthetic? It changes what is in the gas block
steps.action: Look at the stock and then at the top of the gas block. A synthetic-stocked V3 carries gas compensating plugs; a walnut-stocked V3 carries gas exhaust tubes in their place, and its gas block is unvented.
steps.prose: This is the fork that decides which tool you reach for and which instruction you follow — the addendum bound into the front of this manual explicitly replaces step 8 of the manual's own gas piston removal for walnut-stocked guns. The plugs come out with a punch or a wrench; the exhaust tubes come out with a 3/8" open-end wrench, and they go back to a different torque figure. Settle it now, with the gun still assembled, rather than discovering it with a tool already on the part.
steps.caution: Remington: gas exhaust tubes should only be used with unvented gas blocks. Using gas exhaust tubes on a vented gas block can damage the fore-end.
steps.quote: The Remington V3 with walnut stocks is equipped with gas exhaust tubes that replace the gas compensating plugs as shown in the owner’s manual.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Remington® V3™ Autoloading Shotguns — 410252 REV 0526 — Addendum to Owner's Manual for V3 with Walnut Stocks, opening line, p.1

steps.title: Bolt locked open, then look into all three places
steps.action: Engage the safety, pull the operating handle fully rearward to lock the bolt open, and with it locked open visually check the chamber, the ejection port and the magazine to confirm the shotgun is completely unloaded.
steps.prose: The V3 stages a shell on the carrier as well as holding shells in the tube, so there are genuinely three places to satisfy yourself about and the ejection port only shows you one of them. Get light into the loading port from underneath and check that the carrier is bare before you go anywhere near the magazine tube. If the bolt will not lock back, the gun has run out of shells or the bolt release has been pressed — either way, do not assume, cycle it again and watch what comes out.
steps.quote: 4. With the bolt locked open, visually check the chamber, ejection port, and magazine making sure the shotgun is completely unloaded.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Remington® V3™ Autoloading Shotguns — 410252 REV 0526 — To Disassemble the Firearm for Cleaning — To Remove the Barrel, step 4, p.16

steps.title: Magazine cap counter-clockwise, fore-end forward, barrel out
steps.action: Turn the magazine cap counter-clockwise and remove it, slide the fore-end forward off the magazine tube, then hold the barrel above the barrel ring and pull it out of the receiver.
steps.prose: Hold it at the barrel ring, not the muzzle — the ring is the part that has to come off the magazine tube and pulling from the far end cocks it and makes the barrel bind. With cap and fore-end off, the barrel comes away with no force at all; if it resists, the bolt has run forward and the barrel extension is still engaged. Set the barrel down on a soft surface with the gas block uppermost, because that is the assembly you are about to work on.
steps.quote: 5. Remove the magazine cap by turning it counterclockwise. 6. Remove the fore-end from the magazine tube by sliding it forward. 7. While holding the barrel above the barrel ring, pull the barrel from the receiver. See Picture 18.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Remington® V3™ Autoloading Shotguns — 410252 REV 0526 — To Disassemble the Firearm for Cleaning — To Remove the Barrel, steps 5-7, p.16

steps.title: Synthetic stock: both gas compensation plug assemblies out
steps.action: With the barrel off, back both gas compensation plug assemblies out of the top of the gas cylinders, turning counter-clockwise with a punch, an open-end wrench or an adjustable wrench.
steps.prose: There are two of them, side by side in the top of the gas block, and they are usually the tightest fasteners on the gun after a season's shooting — get the tool squarely on before you load it, because a rounded plug is a gunsmith job. They come out counter-clockwise like any thread; the resistance you feel at the start is baked carbon on the threads, not a locking feature. Keep them as a pair and note which cylinder each came from.
steps.quote: 8 With the barrel removed, remove both gas compensation plug assemblies using a punch (or similar tool), or open end wrench or adjustable wrench turning counterclockwise. See Picture 19.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Remington® V3™ Autoloading Shotguns — 410252 REV 0526 — To Disassemble the Firearm for Cleaning — To Remove the Gas Pistons, step 8, p.17

steps.title: Walnut stock: gas exhaust tubes out with a 3/8" wrench instead
steps.action: If your V3 has walnut stocks, ignore the plug step above and instead remove the gas exhaust tubes with a 3/8" open-end wrench, turning counter-clockwise.
steps.prose: Remington's addendum says outright that this replaces step 8 of the manual, so it is not an alternative method — on a walnut gun it is the method. The exhaust tubes are longer than the plugs and stand proud of the block, and they are what vents gas on a gun whose block has no vents of its own. Do not try to substitute the two: fitting exhaust tubes to a vented gas block is the specific mistake the addendum warns damages the fore-end.
steps.quote: To remove the gas pistons on V3’s with walnut stocks for service or cleaning, remove the gas exhaust tubes using a ⅜” open-end wrench turning counter-clockwise.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Remington® V3™ Autoloading Shotguns — 410252 REV 0526 — Addendum to Owner's Manual for V3 with Walnut Stocks — DISASSEMBLY, p.1
steps.warn: NOTE from the addendum: V3s with walnut stocks are also equipped with an unvented gas block on the barrel assembly, and gas exhaust tubes should only be used with unvented gas blocks.

steps.title: Both gas pistons out of the muzzle end of the block
steps.action: With the plugs or tubes out, slide the two gas pistons out of the muzzle end of the gas block.
steps.prose: The pistons come out the front of the block, not the top where the fasteners were — this catches people expecting to lift them out the way the plugs came. They are small, light and identical in appearance, and they go back small-end-first, so note their orientation now rather than guessing later. This is the pair that does the actual work in a VersaPort system, so this is where the carbon is, and it is the part of the V3 that most rewards routine cleaning.
steps.quote: 9. Remove the gas pistons from the muzzle end of the gas block. See Picture 20.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Remington® V3™ Autoloading Shotguns — 410252 REV 0526 — To Disassemble the Firearm for Cleaning — To Remove the Gas Pistons, step 9, p.17

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel off, fore-end off, plugs or exhaust tubes out and both gas pistons out of the block. Receiver, bolt and trigger plate all stay in the gun.
steps.prose: That reaches everything a routine clean needs: the bore, the chamber, the locking notches in the barrel, and the two gas cylinders in the block which are what actually foul on this design. The deeper procedure the book publishes — trigger plate pins out and the trigger plate down out of the receiver, then the bolt forward out of the front of the receiver and the firing pin and ejector rod out of the bolt — is the Deep Clean branch. Remington bounds it there: the V3 is not taken further apart than this manual describes.
steps.quote: CAUTION! Always wear eye protection when handling, disassembling and reassembling the firearm. Not wearing eye protection may lead to personal injury.
steps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Remington® V3™ Autoloading Shotguns — 410252 REV 0526 — To Disassemble the Firearm for Cleaning — caution under the heading, p.16

deepSteps.title: Bolt eased forward, then both trigger plate pins out
deepSteps.action: Hold the operating handle, push the bolt release and let the bolt move slowly forward under control, then tap out both trigger plate pins with a drive punch.
deepSteps.prose: Letting the bolt run home under the action springs with the barrel out slams the bolt head into an empty receiver, which is why the manual has you hold the handle and walk it forward. The two pins are a light push fit and go out with gentle taps; if one needs real force, the plate is loaded against it and wants supporting rather than a bigger hammer. Keep the pins identified — they get put back flush with both sides of the receiver, and swapping them can leave one standing proud.
deepSteps.quote: 10. While holding the operating handle, push the bolt release then slowly let the bolt move forward. 11. Tap out both trigger plate pins with a drive punch. See Picture 21.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Remington® V3™ Autoloading Shotguns — 410252 REV 0526 — To Remove the Trigger Plate Assembly, steps 10-11, p.17

deepSteps.title: Trigger plate straight down out of the receiver
deepSteps.action: Pull the trigger plate downward out of the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: It comes out downward, not rearward as on Remington's older gas guns — the V3's trigger plate drops into a main slot in the underside of the receiver and lifts back into it the same way. Take it out square rather than rocking it, so the hammer and the sear roller do not catch on the receiver walls. Once it is out, set it down hammer uppermost where nothing can press the trigger; it is a live spring-loaded assembly out of the gun.
deepSteps.quote: 12. Remove the trigger plate from the receiver by pulling the trigger plate downward from the receiver. See Picture 22.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Remington® V3™ Autoloading Shotguns — 410252 REV 0526 — To Remove the Trigger Plate Assembly, step 12, p.17

deepSteps.title: Operating handle only comes out at one point of the bolt's travel
deepSteps.action: Press the bolt release and let the bolt assembly come to its forwardmost position, where the operating handle rests on the front edge of the ejection port and lines up with the undercut in its front lower corner. Then pull the handle out and slide the bolt assembly forward out of the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: That undercut is the only place the handle clears, which is why the bolt has to be all the way forward first — this is the step people wrestle with while the bolt sits somewhere in the middle. If it does get stuck part way, the manual's remedy is light rearward pressure on the handle to free it, then let it continue forward under that same light pressure. The bolt then comes out of the FRONT of the receiver, not the back, because there is nothing to take out at the rear on this gun.
deepSteps.aside: On reassembly the same alignment is found by a witness mark on the bolt body — line it up with the centre of the bolt handle slot in the carrier and with that same undercut.
deepSteps.quote: 14. Allow the bolt assembly to come to forwardmost position in the receiver where the operating handle is resting on the front edge of the ejection port. In this position the operating handle will be aligned with the undercut in the front lower corner of the ejection port. See Pictures 23 and 23A.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Remington® V3™ Autoloading Shotguns — 410252 REV 0526 — To Remove the Bolt Assembly, step 14, p.17

deepSteps.title: The firing pin is under spring compression — hold it before you pull the pins
deepSteps.action: Hold the ejector rod and firing pin in place with one hand while you remove the two firing pin retaining pins with the other, then release the spring tension slowly and take out the firing pin, firing pin spring, ejector rod and ejector rod spring.
deepSteps.prose: Two separate springs are held by those retaining pins and both let go the instant the second pin clears, so the hand holding the parts is the safety device here, not a nicety. Wear eye protection and work over a tray or a towel — a V3 firing pin spring that escapes across a workshop is not coming back. Release the pressure over a couple of seconds rather than letting your thumb slip, and lay the four parts out in the order they came free.
deepSteps.quote: WARNING! Use extreme care when removing the firing pin and firing pin retainer, as the firing pin is under compression. Wear eye protection to avoid serious personal injury.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Remington® V3™ Autoloading Shotguns — 410252 REV 0526 — To Disassemble the Bolt Assembly — warning under the heading, p.17

deepSteps.title: Carrier assembly down, then blocker and shell support out of the bolt body
deepSteps.action: Pull the bolt carrier assembly down out of the bolt body, then take the bolt carrier blocker and the shell support out of the bolt body.
deepSteps.prose: The blocker has an assembly boss that seats in a hole in the bolt body, and the shell support sits in its own pocket — both go back one way round only, so look at how they sit before they move. This is as far as the book takes the bolt: the bolt head, the cam pin and the carrier stay as they are. Keep everything from this bolt together, because the shell support in particular is easy to leave behind on a bench and the gun will not feed reliably without it.
deepSteps.quote: 19. Remove the bolt carrier assembly from the bolt body by pulling the bolt carrier assembly down. 20. Remove the bolt carrier blocker and shell support from the bolt body. See Picture 24B.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Remington® V3™ Autoloading Shotguns — 410252 REV 0526 — To Disassemble the Bolt Assembly, steps 19-20, p.18

deepSteps.title: Scrub the gas cylinders with a .40 cal bore brush
deepSteps.action: Spray the gas block, the plug or tube assemblies and the gas pistons with Brite Bore or equivalent and brush the residue off, then run a .40 cal bore brush and cleaner through the inside of both gas cylinders in the block.
deepSteps.prose: The cylinder bores are where a VersaPort V3 actually fouls, and a patch will not touch baked carbon on the cylinder walls — the .40 cal brush is specified because it is the right interference fit for those bores. Work it right through and back rather than poking at the mouth. Dry everything with compressed air or leave it to air dry before oil goes anywhere near, and keep the pistons themselves lightly oiled at most; a wet piston collects the next lot of carbon.
deepSteps.aside: Grease has exactly one home on this gun's bolt: the manual has you lightly apply grease to the cam pin.
deepSteps.quote: Use a .40 cal bore brush and cleaner to thoroughly scrub the inside of the gas cylinders in the gas block.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Remington® V3™ Autoloading Shotguns — 410252 REV 0526 — To Clean the Barrel, step 13, p.18

deepSteps.title: Trigger plate assembly is cleaned whole and never opened
deepSteps.action: Do not take the trigger plate apart. Spray Rem Action Cleaner inside it at the points the manual's Picture 27 marks, dry it fully, then work the trigger and safety through the checks before any oil goes on.
deepSteps.prose: This is the assembly that carries the hammer, the sear roller and the disconnector, and Remington's warning is unusually direct about the consequence of opening it — failure to reassemble it properly is stated as a route to serious injury or death. Clean it by flushing and cycling: solvent in, worked with the trigger and the safety, blown dry, then a light application of oil at the same points. Watch that the trigger returns fully forward after every release while you do it, because that is the check the book builds into this step.
deepSteps.quote: WARNING: Clean the Trigger Plate Assembly as a unit. Do not disassemble.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Remington® V3™ Autoloading Shotguns — 410252 REV 0526 — To Clean the Trigger Plate Assembly — warning under the heading, p.19
deepSteps.warn: Remington: if the trigger does not fully return to the forward position each time it is released, the firearm is NOT in a safe operating condition and must not be used until repaired by a Remington Authorized Repair Center.

deepSteps.title: Action springs and guide rods out, then the receiver flushed
deepSteps.action: Remove the action springs and guide rods, spray and brush everything inside the receiver with Rem Action Cleaner, and dry it thoroughly with compressed air or by leaving it to air dry.
deepSteps.prose: The V3's action springs live in rail slots in the sides of the receiver rather than in the stock tube, so they come out here and they are the reason the inside of the receiver collects residue in two long channels. Take note of how the guide rod heads seat at the bottom of the rail slots — on reassembly each head must sit entirely in its hole before the bolt goes in, or the bolt will not run. Spray the outside of the magazine tube at the same time and scrub it with steel wool if it needs it.
deepSteps.caution: Lubrication must be present on the receiver insert and the wall area behind it — the manual states it is required for proper function of the firearm, not merely good practice.
deepSteps.quote: 1. Remove the action springs and guide rods. See Picture 29.
deepSteps.cite: Owner's Manual — Instruction Book for: Remington® V3™ Autoloading Shotguns — 410252 REV 0526 — To Clean the Receiver Assembly, step 1, p.20

cleaning.name: BARREL, CHOKE & LOCKING NOTCHES
tasks: Brite Bore patch on a jag first, chamber end to muzzle, several passes to lift loose residue
Correct-gauge brush sprayed with Brite Bore, then patches until one comes out with no fouling residue
All shooting residue taken out of the barrel's locking notches with a patch
Rem Oil patch through, then a dry patch behind it; light Rem Oil on the outside of the barrel
Choke tube out, body and both sets of threads brushed clean, dried, lightly oiled and refitted — never fire the gun without one

cleaning.name: GAS BLOCK, PISTONS & PLUGS
tasks: Gas block, plug or exhaust tube assemblies and both gas pistons sprayed with Brite Bore and brushed
Both gas cylinders scrubbed through with a .40 cal bore brush and cleaner
Air dried or blown dry before any lubricant
Light Rem Oil on the gas pistons with a cloth, then the excess taken off with a dry patch
Walnut-stocked guns: check the gas block is the unvented type before the exhaust tubes go back in

cleaning.name: BOLT, TRIGGER PLATE & RECEIVER (deep only)
tasks: Bolt components sprayed with Rem Action Cleaner, brushed if needed, dried, then lightly oiled
Light grease on the cam pin
Trigger plate assembly sprayed at the four points of Picture 27, dried, cycled, then lightly oiled — never disassembled
Action springs and guide rods out; receiver sprayed, brushed and dried inside
Rem Oil on the inside and outside of the receiver, and specifically on the receiver insert and the wall area behind it

reassembly: Bolt first: carrier blocker into the bolt body with its boss in the hole, carrier assembly in, shell support into its pocket, then the firing pin with its spring and the ejector rod with its spring, aligned at their assembly notches so both retaining pins go through.
Gas block, synthetic stocks: pistons in small end first, then the gas compensation plug assemblies clockwise, torqued to 100 in-lbs — or hand tight plus a quick firm pull on the tool.
Gas block, walnut stocks: pistons in small end first, then the gas exhaust tubes clockwise, torqued to 30 in-lb — or hand tight plus a quick firm pull with the 3/8" wrench.
Action springs over the guide rods and into the rail slots on both sides of the receiver, each rod head sitting entirely in the hole at the bottom of its slot before the bolt goes in.

Bolt assembly into the FRONT of the receiver, carrier resting on the front of the action springs; hold the front of the carrier down flush with the front of the receiver — not the bolt head or bolt body.
Operating handle in at the witness mark, with the bolt at the position where it aligns with the undercut in the ejection port.
Hammer cocked against the sear roller, trigger plate up into the main slot, pin holes aligned, both pins in flush with the receiver.
Bolt locked open, barrel in with the barrel ring over the magazine tube, fore-end on, magazine cap hand tight — then run the function test before loading.
fncheck: Unloaded, bolt locked open, chamber and loading port checked: press the bolt release and the bolt should run forward and lock into the firing position without the hammer releasing. With the safety engaged the trigger should not move and the hammer should not release; with it disengaged the trigger should release the hammer and then return fully forward on its own. Then pull the trigger and HOLD it back while you cycle the operating handle rearward and press the bolt release — the hammer must not release while the trigger is still held. Last, with the safety on and the bolt open, confirm the choke tube is present, tight and secure; Remington's instruction is never to discharge the shotgun without one installed.
